facts.raw_span: A man in his 60s developed asthenia, anorexia, and cough
Six days later, he was hospitalized with diffuse bilateral pneumonia
Numerous 3- to 6-mm pseudovesicular papules with superficial crusting were noted on the trunk
The papules were asymptomatic
Within 48 hours the papules evolved to an extensive, but not confluent, purpuric rash

Nasopharyngeal swab using real-time reverse transcriptase–polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) - Diagnostic testing on superficial skin sample for herpes simplex, varicella zoster, and SARS-CoV-2 viruses (all negative)
Immunohistochemical testing for herpes simplex and varicella zoster viruses (negative)
RT-PCR testing of fixed skin tissue for SARS-CoV-2 (negative)
Histologic analysis showed: - Extensive epidermal necrosis with acantholysis
Large multinucleated keratinocytes with ballooning degeneration
Dense perivascular lymphohistiocytic infiltrate with extravasated erythrocytes and eosinophils in superficial dermis
Early-stage vasculitic alterations with endothelial swelling of dermal vessels without fibrinoid necrosis or thrombosis

concepts.why: The patient presented with a purpuric rash and papules, which are consistent with a varicella-zoster virus infection.
The patient was hospitalized with diffuse bilateral pneumonia, which is a common complication of respiratory infections.
The patient's histologic analysis showed early-stage vasculitic alterations, which is consistent with a diagnosis of vasculitis.
The patient presented with a purpuric rash and papules, which are consistent with a diagnosis of erythema multiforme.
The patient's histologic analysis showed dense perivascular lymphohistiocytic infiltrate and early-stage vasculitic alterations, which is consistent with a diagnosis of leukocytoclastic vasculitis.
The patient was hospitalized with diffuse bilateral pneumonia, which is a common complication of acute interstitial pneumonia.
The patient's histologic analysis showed extensive epidermal necrosis and large multinucleated keratinocytes, which is consistent with a diagnosis of toxic epidermal necrolysis.
The patient presented with a purpuric rash and papules, which are consistent with a diagnosis of Stevens-Johnson syndrome.
It explains the extensive epidermal necrosis with acantholysis and the presence of large multinucleated keratinocytes with ballooning degeneration.
